data.name: Satish
data.gender_notes: Satish is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from Sanskrit ‘Sat’ meaning truth and ‘ish’ meaning lord, Satish signifies the existence of truth as the ultimate reality. This name is associated with the Hindu deity, Lord Satish, who is a form of Lord Vishnu, representing the truth and preservation of the universe. The name Satish carries the meaning “Truth, Reality, Existence” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Satish usually hope their child will grow to embody truth, reality, existence and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Satish belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Truth, Reality, Existence.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Satish total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: The name Satish holds significant importance in Hindu culture, expressing the belief in truth as the foundation of all aspects of life. It is believed that Truth is the ultimate reality and that truthfulness in speech and actions leads to peace, happiness and the attainment of life’s goals.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Satish carries deep spiritual significance as it reflects the Hindu concept of 'Satya', or truth, which is one of the essential values upheld in Hinduism. By bestowing this name upon a child, parents express their hope and desire that they will grow up to be truthful in their actions, words and thoughts, and that they will seek and uphold truth as the guiding principle in their lives. Additionally, it is associated with Lord Satish, who is a symbol of the Hindu deity Vishnu’s preservation of truth and the universe.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Satish: Truthful, Pure, and Faithful. Embodying the essence of truth and purity, a Satish continues to remain faithful to their inner self and the divine.

historical_references.reference: Satish Chandra was a renowned historian, born on 12 December 1927 in Allahabad, India. He specialized in medieval Indian history and wrote several books on the subject. One of his most notable works is 'A History of Medieval India: From the Moslem Invasions to the European Advent' published in 1979.

Satish Kumar is a spiritual teacher, author, and editor of 'Resurgence & Ecology' magazine. He was born on 1 November 1954 in Pakistani Punjab. He became a Jain monk at the age of 16 and has been living in a hand-built cob house near the Stonehenge monument since 1977.
